notes: SHIP v1.14.418 - P0 OF PHASE-ENGINE: ONE ANSWER TO WHO IS WORKING. No UI surface. This is the prerequisite for every event PHASE-ENGINE will write, and it closes a live split-brain in the one field that attributes work to a human. THE DEFECT. phantom_current_user_v1 was a SECOND persisted operator identity, independent of the site profile, and deploy_logAudit used it for the actor on every audit entry: actor = identity_getUser() || dep.buildLead || System. So the log that credits work to people read from a source the profile did not own. That contradicts spec section 2 (the actor is currentOperator at time of the event) and the architecture ruling section 8 (do not independently ask different surfaces who the operator is), and it would have failed the spec own acceptance check that a second operator completed step credits that operator. THE DOOR CHANGES, THE TWELVE CALLERS DO NOT. identity_getUser now resolves through PHANTOM_SITE.currentOperator(); identity_setUser writes the profile. Every existing reader keeps calling identity_getUser unchanged. That is the whole blast radius - one function - instead of twelve edits and a thirteenth someone forgets. THE LEGACY KEY IS MIGRATED, NEVER ABANDONED. It holds a name a human typed. It is still read as a fallback for a device that has not migrated, and PHANTOM_SITE.migrate() COPIES it into the profile without deleting it. Dropping it silently would re-credit that person past work to whatever the profile happened to hold. A HAZARD FOUND AND CLOSED IN THE SAME SHIP: v1.14.417 shipped currentOperator() with a read-time fallback to siteLead, on the reasoning that they are usually the same person. That was wrong. This accessor also backs identity_getUser, which gates LEAD-ONLY RBAC actions, so a read-time coalesce would silently grant lead-only actions to whoever held a device whose operator field happened to be empty. The fallback is removed: spec section 2 says the operator DEFAULTS to the Site Lead at Site Setup, which is a value written once and then editable, not a coalesce evaluated on every read. An empty actor now reads as empty. SCOPING RESULT THAT SHAPED THIS SHIP: PHASE-ENGINE is mostly FOLDING, not building. The Event Log the spec describes already exists as phantom_deploy_audit_v1 - append-only, hash-chained via prevHash and hash, tamper-evident through deploy_verifyAuditChain, with a chainReset marker so truncation is visible rather than silent. Owner ruled: fold into it rather than build a second log, keep the existing 2000-entry FIFO cap as an interim safety valve (an amendment to spec section 6.5, which forbids pruning without a verified backup - logged, not silently resolved), and ship all four platform templates. THE GATE CAUGHT A REAL CONSEQUENCE, AND IT CHANGED THE SHIP. The first full run went RED on the backup round-trip: that fixture seeds TWO different operator identities - the profile carries operator E2E and phantom_current_user_v1 carries E2E-TECH - and the test asserted the legacy key wins. That divergence IS the defect being fixed, so the code was right and the test had pinned the old precedence. But the same fixture proves a real-world consequence: on any device where those two stores hold DIFFERENT names, this ship silently changes who gets credited for work. A silent switch of attribution is not something this app does. So migration now RECORDS the divergence - it warns on the console and writes legacyOperatorDiverged onto the profile - without altering the value. The profile still wins by ruling; what changed is that the supersession is visible and inspectable instead of quiet. The legacy key is never destroyed, and a test now pins that it survives the backup round trip. TESTS: six new, eighteen total in the site-profile spec, plus the corrected backup assertion, all green. The one that matters is end to end - with the legacy key deliberately set to a different name, an audit entry written through the real deploy_logAudit credits the PROFILE actor, and the tamper-evident chain still verifies. Also pinned: an unset actor reads empty and never inherits the Site Lead; the legacy key is never written again; and a legacy-only device keeps its attribution. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, braces balanced, CRLF intact, three-stamp lockstep, enforced by the commit hook. No RACK SCENE LOCK term touched. ?legacy=1 unaffected. DEVICE-VERIFY: no visible surface. Confirm v1.14.418, then confirm your name still appears where it did before - the overflow menu label and any deployment sign-off. In the console, identity_getUser() and PHANTOM_SITE.currentOperator() must return the same value, and it must be your name.
